evals.prompt: We're opening forum.quillstack.dev on hosted Discourse in three weeks (Nov 21). It's completely empty right now. Our growth lead wants to create about 15 persona accounts ("Dana from fintech", "Raj the hobbyist" etc.) and have ChatGPT write 60 starter threads and replies so it looks busy on day one. We also planned 14 categories, one per SDK (Go, Python, Node, Java, Rust, .NET...) plus Billing, Roadmap, Jobs, Off-topic. We have a 4-person support team and about 900 Zendesk tickets from the last quarter. Can you write the seeding plan?
evals.expected_output: Refuses persona accounts and bulk AI-generated seed content, replaces them with a founding cohort recruited from real users and seed topics drawn from real tickets posted with consent under real names, cuts the category plan to 3-5 categories with SDKs as tags, and gives a dated cadence to Nov 21 and beyond.
expectations: Refuses creating persona, alt or fake member accounts to seed the forum
Refuses or advises against generating dozens of seed threads or replies with an AI model
Proposes recruiting a founding cohort of named real users (from support, beta or issue history) before the public opening
Proposes seeding from real Zendesk questions, posted either by the original asker or by staff under their own names
Requires the original asker's consent (or anonymised rewriting with consent) before a ticket becomes a public topic
Says seed questions should be answered and marked solved, not left open
Cuts the 14-category plan to roughly 3-5 categories at launch
Moves the per-SDK split from categories to tags
Recommends a Categories homepage (rather than Latest) while the forum is young
Includes a pinned welcome or banner topic saying what the forum is for and how fast staff answer
Gives a dated cadence that works back from the Nov 21 opening (pre-launch weeks, launch week, first 90 days)
Assigns a named owner or rota for a daily pass on unanswered topics during the first 90 days

evals.prompt: Quick sanity check. Our legal counsel wants our new Discourse community (community.ferrolink.io, hosted) to be login-required for the first six months, "until we see what people post". After that we'd flip it public so the threads start ranking on Google, which is the main reason marketing paid for it. Any problem with that plan?
evals.expected_output: Flags that login-required hides the whole site from search for six months and that flipping login-only content public later breaches what members agreed to, so it is close to irreversible; proposes deciding public versus private per category before launch, with restricted categories for contract-covered material and spam controls instead of a site-wide wall.
expectations: States that login-required makes the whole forum invisible to search engines while it is on
Warns that making login-only posts public later conflicts with what existing members expected when they posted (privacy or consent problem)
Calls the plan close to irreversible, or says the content written during the private period cannot simply be flipped public
Recommends deciding public versus private per category before launch rather than site-wide
Suggests a restricted category for content a customer contract or legal concern covers
Points to trust-level sandbox limits, spam detection or approval of suspicious first posts as the control legal actually needs
Notes the search-acquisition goal earns nothing during the six private months
Does not endorse the six-month login-required plan as proposed

evals.prompt: Our Discourse (self-hosted, devs.hallmarkdb.com) is getting hammered: ~40 spam signups a day posting casino and SEO links. Two fixes on the table from my team: (1) put every new topic and reply from everyone into the approval queue, and (2) bulk-promote our 2,000 customers we just imported from Zendesk straight to trust level 3 so the new-user limits stop annoying them. Which one should we do first?
evals.expected_output: Rejects both: approval of every member's posts kills answer time, and bulk TL3 hands spam-prone accounts recategorize powers and followed links. Recommends layered controls - AI spam detection on early posts, watched words and blocked email domains, a TL0-only queue during a wave, a lower per-IP account cap, raising TL1 requirements last - and allows TL1 for verified customers while higher levels are earned or granted individually.
expectations: Advises against sending every post from everyone to the approval queue
Explains that answer time or reply speed is what an all-posts approval queue destroys
Advises against bulk-promoting the 2,000 imported accounts to trust level 3
Notes that links from TL3 posts lose nofollow by default, so bulk TL3 rewards link spammers
Cites at least one concrete TL0 default limit (for example 3 topics and 10 replies on day one, 2 links, or no attachments)
Places raising TL1 requirements after faster controls (spam detection, watched words, TL0-only queue), noting day-one spam posts as TL0
Recommends capping new accounts per IP address (default 3)
Recommends spam detection on new users' first posts (AI spam detection or equivalent)
Limits approval queueing to TL0 or suspicious posts rather than all members' posts
Allows at most TL1 for verified customers (for example through a group) and leaves higher levels to be earned or granted individually
Labels platform defaults as Discourse defaults that the admin can change or should verify in settings
Recommends watched words or blocked email domains as a spam control

evals.prompt: Our forum (community.pellucid.dev, Discourse) gets basically zero Google traffic after 8 months. The SEO agency we hired recommends three things: move it to pellucid.dev/community because subfolders rank better, add QAPage schema to every category including Announcements and Feature Requests, and auto-generate ~200 topics from our docs pages so Google has more to index. They want sign-off Friday. Thoughts?
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on all three with platform and Google sources: no subfolder preference at Google and Discourse recommends subdomains; QAPage only on genuine Q&A pages; scaled generated topics are a spam risk. Gives a real diagnosis path: crawler view, public/canonical/sitemap checks, titles in the asker's words, Solved on support only.
expectations: States that Google has no stated preference between subdomain and subfolder
Notes Discourse recommends a subdomain, or that a subfolder requires maintaining robots.txt at the root by hand
Says QAPage (Q&A) markup belongs only on pages that are one question with answers, per Google
Rejects applying Q&A markup to Announcements and Feature Requests
Recommends enabling Solved only on genuine support or Q&A categories
Rejects auto-generating ~200 topics from docs, citing scaled or low-value content risk
Suggests auditing the crawler view of a topic (for example with ?print or the crawler header)
Suggests checking that solved topics are public, canonical and present in the sitemap
Advises topic titles written in the asker's own words, because title and first post become the search snippet
Labels claims by source (Google versus Discourse versus practitioner) rather than presenting all as fact
Does not promise a traffic outcome from the changes

evals.prompt: Need a reality check for our exec review. Our Discourse forum has 3,100 members and 41 categories. Last month 38% of new topics had no reply after a week, and our two DevRel people wrote about 80% of all answers. The CEO thinks we need paid ads to bring more people in. What would you change in the next quarter?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses staffing and structure, not reach: unanswered topics and staff-written answers come first; merges dead categories, sets a daily triage owner, uses Solved and the unsolved filter, grows TL2/TL3 helpers and promotes TL4 by hand; rejects ads as the first move; sets Discourse-report metrics and a stop rule.
expectations: Identifies the unanswered-topic rate as a staffing or triage problem before any traffic problem
Advises against paid ads as the first move while 38% of topics go unanswered
Recommends merging categories with no recent new topics (for example none in 30 days)
Assigns a daily pass on unanswered or unsolved topics to a named owner
Recommends Solved and the unsolved filter as the triage queue for support topics
Proposes growing non-staff helpers through trust levels, and promoting proven helpers to TL4 by hand
Sets a time-to-first-reply target (for example a median under 24 hours)
Tracks the share of solutions written by non-staff members
Names Discourse admin reports (time to first response, topics with no response, trust level growth) as the data source
Includes a stop or fold-back rule if non-staff solutions and TL2 growth do not move
Does not treat the 3,100 member count as evidence of health

evals.prompt: Our devrel team posts about four release announcements a week on our Discourse and bumps them a couple of times so they stay at the top. They never show up in the Hot tab and barely appear in the weekly summary email. How does Discourse actually decide what's hot or top, and what should we do differently?
evals.expected_output: Explains Latest as bump order, Hot as likes plus distinct likers and posters over the last 7 days decayed by age (gravity 1.2), Top as views, first-post likes, likes per post and post count with a 10-post bonus, and the summary email built from popular topics with category suppression; says bumping mainly moves Latest; moves announcements to their own category, adds a weekly ritual topic, and labels claims as Discourse-sourced.
expectations: Says bumping mainly moves a topic on Latest and does little for Hot or Top
Explains Hot as driven by likes and the number of distinct people liking or posting, decayed by topic age, over recently active topics (about the last 7 days)
Explains Top as weighting views, first-post likes and likes per post, with a boost for longer discussions (around 10+ posts)
Says staff-only or announcement topics with few member likes or replies score low
Recommends a separate Announcements category for release posts
Says Announcements can be excluded from the summary email with its suppress-categories setting
Recommends a member-participation surface such as a weekly ritual topic instead of more announcements
Labels the ranking explanation as coming from Discourse's own code or docs, not guesswork
Recommends reducing self-bumping

evals.prompt: Two things for our Discourse forum at forum.tallyhq.com: we want users to log in with their existing Tally app account and see related forum threads inside our docs pages. Also, someone on the team says we should just have used Discord instead - should we switch?
evals.expected_output: Routes SSO with the product account and docs embedding to samber/developer-platform-skills@developer-portal-design, and the Discord-versus-forum venue question to samber/developer-relations-skills@developer-community-launch, without doing either job itself.
expectations: Routes the single-sign-on and docs-embedding work to samber/developer-platform-skills@developer-portal-design
Routes the forum-versus-Discord venue decision to samber/developer-relations-skills@developer-community-launch
Does not write DiscourseConnect or embed configuration steps itself
Does not decide the Discord-versus-Discourse switch itself
Offers to continue with forum operations (categories, trust levels, seeding or SEO) once those are settled
